name: Bambu Lab R1
tagline: Bambu Lab's first laser: enclosed 55W CO₂ with a 600 × 300 mm bed, camera alignment and an optional 3 m conveyor
tldr: The R1 is Bambu Lab's first standalone laser cutter, announced on September 22, 2026 and not yet delivered: pre-orders are open, with shipping now expected in November 2026. It is an enclosed 55W CO₂ machine with a 600 × 300 mm bed, up to 1,000 mm/s, a camera and sensor system for alignment and focus, and an optional conveyor for material up to 3 m long. Bambu Lab lists $2,499 / €2,499. Early hands-on reviews exist, but no buyer has received one yet, and specs, software and prices may still change before delivery.
mainObjective: Enclosed 55W CO₂ cutting and engraving for makers already in the Bambu Lab ecosystem

priceRange.note: Pre-order price, Bambu Lab store (Oct 2026): $2,499 / €2,499 for the R1 alone, which the EU store estimated on 29 October would ship around November 9, 2026; EU bundles €3,329 with riser base and conveyor and €3,559 with rotary as well (sold out); US bundles reported at $3,289 and $3,499. Not delivered yet; prices may change.

cut: Plywood up to 18 mm (Bambu Lab figure)
Acrylic up to 20 mm (Bambu Lab figure)
cannot: Use without exhaust or air purifier

pros: 600 × 300 mm enclosed CO₂ bed at $2,499, below most enclosed 55W rivals
Bird's-eye and toolhead cameras, distance laser and XY encoders for alignment and auto-focus
Optional conveyor takes material up to 3 m long, and the riser base handles taller objects
cons: Not delivered yet: shipping slipped from October to November 2026 and there is no long-term feedback
Bambu Suite only at launch; LightBurn support is promised without a date
Class 1 safety is lost once the riser base or conveyor is fitted, and the purifier, fire extinguisher and encoder are extra
beginnerNotes: The R1 is announced but not yet in buyers' hands. If you need a CO₂ laser now, compare it with machines already shipping, such as the xTool P2S. Plan for ventilation: the R1 needs an exhaust to the outside or Bambu Lab's air purifier, sold separately.
proTips: Wait for the first deliveries and independent cutting tests before committing a business to it. If you plan to cut long parts, price the riser base and conveyor bundle from the start, and remember that the machine is no longer Class 1 with them fitted: eye protection becomes mandatory.
primaryUse: Enclosed 55W CO₂ for cutting and engraving wood, acrylic and leather, with long-material feed

faq.question: When will the Bambu Lab R1 ship, and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: Pre-orders opened on September 22, 2026 at $2,499 in the US and €2,499 in Europe. Bambu Lab first announced shipping in October 2026; in October its stores showed estimated shipping dates in November 2026 (around November 9 on the EU store on October 29). Until machines are delivered, specs, prices and dates may still change.

faq.question: What can the R1 cut?
faq.answer: Bambu Lab quotes up to 18 mm plywood and 20 mm acrylic, plus leather, paper and fabric. It also engraves glass, stone and coated metal. These are manufacturer figures; we have not measured cutting speeds or thicknesses yet.

faq.question: R1 or xTool P2S?
faq.answer: Both are enclosed 55W CO₂ machines with a bed around 600 × 300 mm and camera placement. The P2S has been on sale for longer and supports LightBurn; the R1 costs less at launch and fits into Bambu Lab's software and MakerWorld. Until the R1 ships and is tested, the P2S is the safer choice.

editorialDepth.advantages: On paper, the R1 brings a full-size enclosed CO₂ laser to Bambu Lab's ecosystem at an aggressive launch price: a 600 × 300 mm bed, 1,000 mm/s, cameras, distance sensing and encoders for automatic alignment and focus, plus a conveyor for long parts. Makers who already use Bambu Lab printers and MakerWorld get one account and one software for both.
editorialDepth.limitations: The machine is not delivered yet and shipping has already slipped once. Software is limited to Bambu Suite until LightBurn support arrives, and the enclosure loses its Class 1 rating with the riser base or conveyor. Ventilation, fire suppression and the precision encoder cost extra, so the real budget is higher than $2,499.

standoutFeatures.title: Camera and sensor alignment
standoutFeatures.body: A bird's-eye camera, toolhead cameras, a distance laser for focus and XY encoders place designs and adjust focus automatically.

standoutFeatures.title: Material up to 3 m long
standoutFeatures.body: With the optional riser base and conveyor, the R1 feeds stock up to 3,000 mm long through the 600 × 300 mm bed.

standoutFeatures.title: Bambu Lab ecosystem
standoutFeatures.body: The R1 uses the same Bambu Lab account, Bambu Suite software and MakerWorld project library as the brand's 3D printers.
